expectations.text: The skill discovers and reads the existing rules file before writing anything
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 1: 'Scanned .claude/rules/ and found one rules file: .claude/rules/team-standards.md (scoped to src/**/*). No other rules files or top-level CODING_STANDARDS.md found.' Step 2 counts existing enforcement blocks (all 0).

expectations.text: It asks which section the rule belongs in (or suggests Code Style)
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 3: 'The file has three sections: Code Style, Debugging, Testing. The user's request is about removing console.log debugging calls before committing. The Debugging section is the closest thematic match -- it already contains a rule about using a logger utility instead of raw console.* calls. Suggested placement: Debugging section, as a new bullet after the existing logger rule.'

expectations.text: The rule text is one clear imperative sentence, not a paragraph or multi-sentence explanation
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 4 and output file show the rule text: 'Do not commit console.log, console.debug, console.info, or console.warn calls.' -- one clear imperative sentence.

expectations.text: The rule is classified as T1 (console.log has a clear syntactic signature)
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 5: 'The pattern console.(log|debug|info|warn)( is a syntactic signature that is always wrong in committed code, regardless of context... Classification: T1 (deterministic, pre-commit).' Output file shows tier: T1.

expectations.text: The enforcement block has a regex pattern matching console.log
expectations.evidence: Output file enforcement block contains: pattern: "console\\.(log|debug|info|warn)\\s*\\("

expectations.text: The rule is appended to an appropriate section, not dumped at the end of the file
expectations.evidence: Output file shows the new rule and enforcement block appear under '## Debugging' section, after the existing logger utility rule and before '## Testing'. Not dumped at the end.

expectations.text: Budget checks run after generating the block
expectations.evidence: Transcript Step 8 shows a full budget check with per-file breakdown and aggregated totals after adding the rule: 'Total T3 rules: 0', 'Scopeless T3: 0', 'Critical T3: 0'. All within limits.

claims.claim: Excluded console.error from the ban since it may have legitimate production use
claims.evidence: Transcript Step 4: 'Does not include console.error since that may have legitimate production use.' This is a thoughtful design decision.
Transcript lists 'Implicit stable ID: team-standards:debugging:t1' which follows the file:section:tier convention.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are comprehensive for this eval. The section-placement and budget-check assertions are particularly good discriminators.
